L110:     * cite52†Sitemap L111: # Military and Overseas Voters
L112: 
L113: Massachusetts citizens who are in the military or overseas can vote in all elections.
L114: 
L115: Citizens deployed, stationed outside of Massachusetts, or living overseas have their right to vote protected by the cite53†Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act†www.fvap.gov (UOCAVA).
L116: If you are a military or overseas voter, you are exempt from voter registration requirements in Massachusetts. In order to get your ballot, you simply need to submit an absentee ballot application.
L117: ## Military Voters
L118: 
L119: You can vote by absentee ballot if:
L120: 
L121:   * You’re a member of the United States Military on active duty.
L122:   * You’re a dependent family member of someone on active duty.
L123: 
L124: If you’re a member of the military stationed in Massachusetts, you can register to vote in Massachusetts.
L125: 
L126: If you lived in Massachusetts before being called to active duty and you haven’t registered elsewhere, you can vote by absentee ballot in Massachusetts elections.
L127: Members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Coast Guard (including reservists on active duty), and the merchant marine are all eligible military voters.
L128: ## Overseas Citizens
L129: 
L130: If you’re a United States citizen living overseas, you can vote in U.S. elections. You can vote using the address from your last residence in the United States. If you’re a citizen who has never lived in the U.S., you can vote from your qualifying parent’s last U.S. address.
L131: ## Applying for your Ballot
L132: 
L133: If you’d like to get an absentee ballot, you can:
L134: 
L135:   * Apply with the cite54†Federal Post Card Application†www.fvap.gov or
L136:   * Apply with the cite55†Massachusetts Absentee Ballot Application or
L137:   * Send a written request for an absentee ballot to your local election office
L138: 
L139: Any application has to be sent to your local election office. The signature on your application needs to be able to be compared to your hand-written signature. Typed signatures won’t be accepted.
L140: Your absentee ballot application is valid until December 31 of the year that you submit it. You will need to submit a new absentee ballot application every year in which you want to vote.
L141: 
L142: Absentee ballot applications must reach your local election office by 5 p.m. on the 5^{th} business day before an election. If you miss the deadline to apply for a ballot, you can vote using a cite56†Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot†www.fvap.gov .
L143: ## Voting
L144: 
L145: You’ll receive a ballot with the same races as all other Massachusetts voters.
L146: 
L147: You can choose to receive your ballot through an online portal, by fax, or by mail. There is a space on the Federal Post Card Application where you can mark how you’d like to receive your ballot. You can also choose to return your ballot by email/online, by fax, or by mail.
L148: If you do not receive your ballot in time, you can submit a Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot (FWAB) by email or fax. A FWAB is a blank ballot that you can use for any election.
L149: ## Returning Your Ballot
L150: 
L151: Ballot deadlines are different depending on the type of election and how you return your ballot. Deadlines for electronic return (email, online, and fax) may differ from deadlines for ballots returned by mail. Below is a list of deadlines by type of election.
L152: 
L153: For local elections, you can check with your local election office about what time polls close.
L154: 
L155: ### State and Federal Elections
L156: #### Regular Election
L157: 
L158:   * Electronic return:
L159:     * 8 p.m. on Election Day
L160:   * Mailed from inside the U.S.:
L161:     * Postmarked by Election Day
L162:     * Received by 5 p.m. on the third day after Election Day
L163:   * Mailed from outside the United States:
L164:     * Postmarked by Election Day
L165:     * Received by 5 p.m. on the tenth day after Election Day
L166: #### Special Election
L167: 
L168:   * Electronic return:
L169:     * 8 p.m. on Election Day
L170:   * Mailed from inside the U.S.:
L171:     * 8 p.m. on Election Day
L172:   * Mailed from outside the United States:
L173:     * Postmarked by Election Day
L174:     * Received by 5 p.m. on the tenth day after Election Day
L175: 
L176: ### State and Federal Primaries
L177: 
L178: All primary ballots must be received by 8 p.m. on Election Day.
L179: 
L180: ### City Elections
L181: #### General Election
L182: 
L183:   * Electronic return:
L184:     * Close of polls on Election Day
L185:   * Mailed from inside the U.S.:
L186:     * Close of polls on Election Day
L187:   * Mailed from outside the United States:
L188:     * Postmarked by Election Day
L189:     * Received by 5 p.m. on the tenth day after Election Day
L190: 
L191: #### Preliminary Election
L192: 
L193: All preliminary election ballots must be received by close of polls on Election Day.
L194: 
L195: ### Town Elections
L196: 
L197: All town election ballots must be received by the close of polls on Election Day.
L198: ## Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot
L199: 
L200: The cite56†Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot (FWAB)†www.fvap.gov is a ballot of last resort. If you were not able to apply or receive your ballot in time, you may submit a FWAB.
L201: 
L202: The FWAB is a blank ballot, which you may use to vote for any candidates or ballot questions.
L203: 
L204: You may use a FWAB for any election, whether or not you have applied for a ballot. A FWAB may be submitted by mail, email or fax.
L205: ## Resources
L206: 
L207: The Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) is a federal agency which exists to help military and overseas citizens exercise their voting rights.
L208: 
L209: Visit cite57†www.FVAP.gov†www.fvap.gov for information and forms, including the Federal Post Card Application and the Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot.
